packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING - packet-06

Exposure statement: no outside source, catalogue, edition or earlier transcription was consulted. No
identification of work or author is attempted. (Process note: one directory listing of the packet folders was
run to see image filenames; packet.json was not opened.) One line of the text itself quotes a verse as a
grammatical example (image-004 L5); I transcribed it from the letters and did not look anything up.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview of the inside of a book cover. A parchment leaf is pasted down as a pastedown beneath a
  pink/red leather turn-in; the leaf shows two columns of small, very heavily abbreviated cursive-influenced
  book hand, about 35-38 lines visible per column. A modern paper label with the number "3614." (rotated) is
  pasted over the inner edge of both columns; several small square parchment tabs (former fastening points) cover
  patches of text; the lower lines of both columns are damaged by a fold, tears and the board edge. The right
  edge of the right column is cut off by the cover edge / crop.
- Left column: no heading; begins mid-sentence. One faint line of smaller writing above its top line at the
  right ("ut ... (et) alb(us) ..."), apparently an addition or the tail of a preceding line.
- Right column: opens with an enlarged red initial (round letter, with a red pen-flourish descending the margin,
  read as "D"/"O" shape) followed by "E" in ink, i.e. a new section begins here.
- Small red paraph marks / red-touched capitals mark sentence or section openings inside the text. No running
  title, no underlining seen. Some interlinear corrections (small superscript words) in the left column.
- images 008-011: a different view - a long horizontal strip showing small pieces of the same or a similar
  script visible in windows/gaps (probably the pastedown or sewing-guard strips seen at the spine edge), partly
  blurred, plus one line of a larger later cursive. Only scraps are legible.
- Tentative interpretation only: continuous grammatical prose about which word "governs" (regit) which case,
  with short Latin example sentences.

SPANS SELECTED
Right column opening (image-003 L1-13, continued in image-005); left column middle (image-004 L2-16; overlaps
with image-002 last three lines and image-006 first lines); two lines of a verb list from image-006. Unread:
left column top (image-002, only spot-read), the lower third of both columns (images 006, 007 - damaged), the
right-hand edge of the right column (cropped in every image), and nearly all of the strip images 008-011.

--- RIGHT COLUMN, opening ---

image-005 L4: [under label]retaq(ue)(?) ipar(um)(?) sub(stanti)am ad actu(m). actus regit sub(stanti)am. [cropped]
image-005 L5: [..]c. sic d(icendum?). e(st) de iniectione. q(uod) no(n) reg(it). s(ed) (con)i(un)c(t)io(?) tal(is) t[..]cata(?) [cropped]
image-005 L6: [..](et) reg(u)n(t). Vbi gra(tia). heu m(ihi?). dolor e(st) m(ihi?). heu me. dolor h(abe)t [cropped]

image-004 L11: Aut a(m)bo cadu(n)t in supp(osito). (et) tu(n)c acc(usatiu)i a(m)bo r(eguntu)r ex ui t(ra)nsicionis aut unus cadit
image-004 L12: in supp(osito). alt(er) in app(osito) (et) tu(n)c r(eguntu)r ex diu(er)sis uirib(us), ille qui t(ra)nsit(?) in supp(osito) fit t(ra)nsi
image-004 L13: [..] q(ui) u(er)o remanet(?) i(n) app(osito) fiet(?) [illegible] (et) reg(itur) ex ui [illegible]. ut fiat(?). ut facio te milite(m)
image-004 L14: (con)u(er)tendo act(iuu)m in passiuu(m) dicam(us) tu fis a me miles. Si au(tem) uni(us) acc(usatiu)us mutet(ur) i(n) n(omina)t(iuu)m

image-006 L5: [under tab] [..]cu(m) uno acc(usatiu)o. Vn(de) u(er)s(us). Flagito posco peto moneo doceo rogo celo. In[..]
image-006 L6: [..]or(?) interrogo calceo cingo. acc(usatiu)os geminos h(ec) u(er)ba requir(un)t. S(i) au(tem) pas[..]

--- STRIP IMAGES 008-011 (scraps only; fragments separated by gaps, order uncertain) ---

image-010 L2: [..]. quot(?) [illegible] u(er)b(u)m absolutu(m). Ite(m)(?) au(tem) q(uod)
image-010 L3: [..] Vno m(odo) cu(m) in supp(osit)o intellig[..](?) u(er)b(u)m t(ra)nsi[..]
image-010 right scrap: [..]oc supp(osi)t[..] / [..]tonis(?) reg(it). / subie[..] (et) uni(us?) / reg(it). Vocat(?) h[..]
image-011 right scrap L1: s(ed) hoc dis[..]e(?) conu(er)s[..]
image-011 right scrap L2: cop(u)l(at)e(?). (et) h(ec) cop(u)la no(n)
image-011 right scrap L3: [..]te post ut ego su(m)
image-011 right scrap L4: [c]op(u)l(at)e(?) reg(it). hic nod(um?) q(uod)
image-010/011 larger later cursive line across the strip: "Absolue(?) [illegible] ..." - not read.

LIMITATIONS
- The script abbreviates grammatical terms to one or two letters with superscripts (r', acc', supp', app', t'nsi').
  Expansions in parentheses are proposals; in particular "r(egit)/r(egitur)/r(eguntur)" and the case names are
  inferred from the letter + mark, and "sub(stanti)am" could be another sub- word (e.g. supposition-related).
- Every right-column line is cropped at the right, and lines 7-11 lose their beginnings under the paper label.
- Lower lines of both columns (fold, tabs, tears) are not reliably readable at this resolution.
- A flat, higher-resolution image of the pastedown without the label, and sharper images of the spine strip,
  would be needed for a continuous reading.
